newsitem.title: FRANCE: GEC-Alsthom partners study Framatome merger.
newsitem.headline: GEC-Alsthom partners study Framatome merger.

text.p: Alcatel Alsthom and Britain's General Electric Co Plc said on Friday they planned to study a possible merger between their joint venture engineering company GEC-Alsthom and France's state-controlled nuclear power station manufacturer Framatome.
The French and British governments have been informed of the plan to explore a merger, the two electrical groups said in a joint statement.
"It is envisaged that shares in the new group would be held by the present shareholders of the companies involved, bearing in mind their respective contributions," the statement said.

Alcatel owns some 44 percent of Framatome which is one of the world's leading builders of power stations and suppliers of nuclear fuel. The French company has long said it wanted to acquire control of Framatome or would consider pulling out.

A merger between GEC-Alsthom, whose engineering products include France's high-speed trains, and Framatome would establish a group with annual sales of more than 12 billion European Currency Units ($15 billion) and 90,000 employees worldwide, the statement said.
The French government said afterwards it had given its approval for the public shareholders in Framatome to go ahead with the merger discussions.
